entries.note: Can I have some more pizza? Yeah, knock yourself out! (go ahead)
entries.definition: An informal way of saying 'go ahead' or 'help yourself', giving someone permission to do or take as much as they like.
entries.example: Can I have some more pizza? Yeah, knock yourself out!

entries.note: Bursting with flavours
entries.definition: Used of food or drink that is full of strong, delicious taste.
entries.example: The tomatoes from the market in Grenoble were bursting with flavour, so we simply ate them with olive oil.

entries.key: mind if i grab the last
entries.term: Mind if I grab the last one?
entries.note: Mind if I grab the last…?
entries.definition: A casual, polite way of asking whether you may take the last remaining portion of something, such as food.
entries.example: Mind if I grab the last slice of tart before Auryn and Ella spot it?
entries.pronunciation: /maɪnd ɪf aɪ ɡræb ðə lɑːst wʌn/

entries.note: The behind-the-towel dance
entries.definition: The awkward wriggling and hopping people do on a beach to change into or out of swimwear while hidden behind a towel.
entries.example: On the beach, Papa did the behind-the-towel dance, hopping about as he tried to pull on his swimming trunks.

entries.note: she wore a cast (not plaster one though).
entries.definition: A hard protective casing, nowadays often made of fibreglass rather than plaster, that holds a broken bone in place while it heals.
entries.example: Ella wore a cast on her wrist for six weeks after falling off her bike.

entries.note: whooping cough (coqueluche)
entries.definition: Whooping cough (coqueluche) is a contagious bacterial infection of the airways that causes violent coughing fits, often ending in a loud 'whoop' as the person breathes in.
entries.example: The pharmacist reminded Maman that babies should be vaccinated against whooping cough as early as possible.

entries.note: He’s deadheading the flowers
entries.definition: To remove faded or dead flower heads from a plant so that it produces more blooms.
entries.example: He's deadheading the flowers so they keep blooming until the first frosts.

entries.term: to get to the bottom of something
entries.note: I’ll get to the bottom of it, trust me (élucider, mettre au clair)
entries.definition: To find out the real cause of a problem or mystery, so as to clear it up completely (élucider, mettre au clair).
entries.example: Someone has been hiding Ella's shoes again, but I'll get to the bottom of it, trust me.

entries.note: So fast forward a few more years…
entries.definition: To skip ahead in time when telling a story, jumping over the events in between.
entries.example: So fast forward a few more years, and Auryn is packing his bags for university.

entries.note: right on cue (at just the right moment)
entries.definition: At exactly the right moment, as if it had been planned.
entries.example: I was just saying we were all starving when, right on cue, Papa walked in with croissants.

entries.note: next to no time (almost immediately or very quickly)
entries.definition: Almost immediately or very quickly, after hardly any time at all.
entries.example: The pasta was ready in next to no time, so Auryn and Ella barely had to wait.

entries.theme: Efficiency & work + at work + with students
entries.note: Give me some heads-up if you hear anything special about the new reform
entries.definition: An early warning or piece of advance information about something that is about to happen.
entries.example: Give me a heads-up if you hear anything special about the new reform.

entries.key: start a new line begin a new
entries.theme: Efficiency & work + at work + with students
entries.note: Start a new line / begin a new §
entries.definition: To begin writing on a fresh line, as when starting a new paragraph (marked with the symbol §).
entries.example: Remember to start a new line whenever you move on to a different idea in your essay.

entries.note: The top brass (= les gros bonnets) or the brass hats
entries.definition: The most senior officials in an organisation, such as the army or a ministry (les gros bonnets); also called the brass hats.
entries.example: The top brass at the ministry have finally agreed to postpone the reform.

entries.note: At times she can’t resist pushing my buttons, he knows exactly how to annoy me.
entries.definition: To deliberately say or do things that you know will annoy or upset someone.
entries.example: At times he can't resist pushing my buttons; he knows exactly how to annoy me.

entries.note: She couldn’t help dancing as soon as the brass band started playing
entries.definition: A group of musicians who play brass instruments such as trumpets, trombones and tubas, often with drums.
entries.example: She couldn't help dancing as soon as the brass band started playing.

entries.note: Expressing SURPRISE or DISBELIEF I thought that you, of all people, would believe me; I can’t, for the life of me, understand what he sees in her; We were flabbergasted when we saw how much the repair cost
entries.definition: Extremely surprised or shocked, almost unable to believe something.
entries.example: We were flabbergasted when we saw how much the repair cost.

entries.key: we ve stopped for cheeky macdonald
entries.note: We’ve stopped for cheeky MacDonald
entries.definition: A quick, slightly indulgent and unplanned meal at McDonald's, enjoyed as a small treat.
entries.example: We stopped for a cheeky McDonald's on the way back from Grenoble.

entries.note: Paint stripper = décapant
entries.definition: A chemical product (décapant) used to remove old paint or varnish from a surface.
entries.example: Papa used paint stripper to take the old varnish off the wooden shutters.

entries.key: we re working on the chicken coop especially on the pop hole door
entries.note: We’re working on the chicken coop, especially on the pop hole (door)
entries.definition: A small opening or door in a chicken coop that lets the hens go in and out.
entries.example: We're working on the chicken coop, especially on the pop hole, so the hens can get out.
